# Computer Hardware

## Core ideas and reasoning

Hardware consists of physical components. Input devices capture data and commands; output devices present results. The CPU fetches, decodes and executes instructions. Its control unit coordinates operations while the arithmetic and logic unit performs arithmetic and logical comparisons. Registers hold small amounts of data and instructions needed immediately. Main memory supplies current instructions and data; secondary storage retains files for later use. RAM is normally volatile and loses its contents without power. ROM or flash firmware stores startup instructions; modern firmware may be updateable. Cache reduces average access time by keeping frequently needed data near the processor. A device's suitability depends on the task: a scanner captures a document image, OCR software recognises text in it, and a plotter or large-format printer can produce large technical drawings. Distinguish capacity, access speed and portability when comparing storage. Do not claim that every printer works by impact or that secondary storage replaces working memory. Describe an operation and the reason for choosing it.

## Worked practice

### Example 1

Explain the role of the ALU in a CPU.

The arithmetic and logic unit performs arithmetic operations such as addition and logical comparisons such as testing whether one value exceeds another.

### Example 2

Distinguish RAM from secondary storage.

RAM holds active programs and data and is normally volatile. Secondary storage retains files without power and usually has greater capacity but slower access.

### Example 3

Choose an input device and software for converting printed text to editable text.

Use a scanner to capture an image and optical character recognition software to recognise its characters. A scanner alone produces an image, not necessarily editable text.

### Example 4

Explain the functions of the ALU and the control unit in the CPU.

The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations. The control unit coordinates operations and controls instruction execution and data movement.

### Example 5

List two soft-copy output devices.

A monitor and speakers. They present visual and audio output without producing a permanent paper copy.

## Check your reasoning

Explain why the method applies before calculating or naming a result. Compare with a contrasting case. For calculations carry units, keep intermediate precision, then check by substitution, conservation or a second route. Describe observations separately from their explanation.
